claim: For every integer \(n\ge 2\), let \(C_n\) be the \(2n\)-point crown with minimal points \(a_i\), maximal points \(b_i\), and strict relations \(a_i<b_i\) and \(a_i<b_{i-1}\), with indices in \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\). Let \(F_2(C_n)=\{(x,y)\in C_n\times C_n:x\ne y\}\) carry the induced product order. Then the first-coordinate projection \(\pi_1:F_2(C_n)\to C_n\) is a weak homotopy equivalence. Consequently \(F_2(C_n)\) has \(2n(2n-1)\) points, is a finite model of \(S^1\), and \(|\mathcal K(F_2(C_n))|\simeq S^1\).

correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 the first projection from the deleted diagonal in C_n x C_n has contractible inverse images of all minimal open sets. Minimal-point fibers are crown-minus-one-point paths. Maximal-point fibers admit the explicit uniform beat sequence recorded in RESULT.md, leaving another crown-minus-one-point path. McCord's basis-like-cover theorem therefore gives a weak homotopy equivalence. The order complex of C_n is a cycle, so the configuration finite space has weak type S^1. The included checker reconstructs all posets and verifies every fiber contracts for n=2,...,12, but finite testing is only a stress test and is not used to justify the universal quantifier.

value.rationale: The finite crown is the canonical minimal finite circle model, and deleting the diagonal from a product is the basic two-particle configuration operation. The theorem shows that the natural forgetful map remains a weak equivalence for every crown size, matching the circle phenomenon by a direct finite-space argument. This is structurally motivated, parameter-uniform, and reusable; it is not an arbitrary finite census or a renaming of a known statement.
